Yeah you're right about the double edged thing.

Take entertainment as an example. Now that live TV is dying (for anything other than live events like sports), everyone has the ability to binge watch what they want when they want to.

Think about this for a second, just a decade or two ago most people were forced to watch what their TV channel happened to be playing at that moment. That means that you would watch:

  1. Whatever the TV company chose to put on their roster
  2. Whatever season/episode they could be bothered playing
  3. Finding new TV shows was NOT as simple as scrolling through a huge library or even hearing about it on reddit. You had to fucking hear about it through newspapers or friends, or hope you'd stumble upon it as it happened to be aired.

Things are so much better now, right? No. I am scared that this trend is already leading to a kind of entertainment decadence. Think about it, in the 90s and early 00s, given the aforementioned conditions you'd naturally end up watching a lot of mediocre TV because there's nothing better on. That doesn't happen any more. Nothing take your fancy on Netflix? Try Hulu. Nothing there? Go on youtube and find some genuinely laugh-out-loud content. But what happens when basically everything you watch is brilliant?

You lose sight of what 'good' is. You'll start poking holes in decent to very good things all the time, because your standards are now insanely high. In 2015 you can demand to be fully entertained all of the time, because something better is just a click away. This leads to people nit-picking everything. Awesome new transformers movie that would make any person from the 90s head explode? Meh, shit. Lazy. Micheal Bay blah blah blah. Or video games - boooooring another Call of Duty, Ghosts is so SHIT amarite? Fallout 4? Meh, the graphics are always shit in those games. ARE YOU KIDDING ME?

This is why the internet is the way it is. We have become utterly decadent after just a few short years of having the entire world's library of entertainment at our finger tips. And it's only gonna get worse.
